claims.statement: Meta documents an Instagram User access token, issued through Business Login for Instagram in short-lived and long-lived forms, that an app uses against Instagram API with Instagram Login endpoints.

sources.supports: short-lived Instagram User access token which your app can use to access Instagram API with Instagram Login endpoints
sources.locator: Business Login for Instagram, Step 1 to Step 3

claims.statement: Meta documents that the Instagram User access token is returned in the access_token value of a data entry of the JSON response of the https://api.instagram.com/oauth/access_token authorization code exchange (short-lived), and as the access_token member of the response of https://graph.instagram.com/access_token (long-lived). This is recorded for the Instagram User access token only.

sources.supports: Capture the access_token value. This is the user’s short-lived Instagram User access token which your app can use to access Instagram API with Instagram Login endpoints.
sources.locator: Business Login for Instagram, Step 2. Exchange the Code For a Token

sources.supports: On success, your app receives a JSON response with your app user’s long-lived access token, the token type, and the expiration.
sources.locator: Business Login for Instagram, Step 3. Get a long-lived access token

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Only existence is established; the page gives no token grammar and its examples are truncated placeholders.

The Instagram Login flow uses separate endpoints and an Instagram app secret. Whether its tokens are a different family from meta:user-access-token, or the same kind of token, is not stated; kept separate pending a page that settles it.
The page states no Authorization header form for calls to Instagram API with Instagram Login endpoints; none is recorded.
